name: Lycium-rehmannia pills (Chinese herbal formula)
short: Few data. Meta-analysis of 15 trials (dry eye; pills added to eye drops): eyelid inflammation and congestion did not differ significantly from eye drops alone. Seriousness not reported.
text: Few data. In a 2020 meta-analysis of 15 randomized trials (1,222 patients with dry eye) comparing the pills taken with Western eye drops against the eye drops alone, adverse reactions such as eyelid inflammation (odds ratio 1.00) and congestion (odds ratio 0.55, not statistically significant) did not differ significantly between the groups. The abstract does not give how many people had each reaction or whether any were serious, does not list the pills' herbs or give a Chinese name, and notes that the trials were limited in quantity and quality. No other human safety data for a product of this name were found. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
